course: Although the format of the course didn’t agree with me (my own personal shortcomings with rote memorisation) I really enjoyed the entire course, feel that I have learned quite a lot, and do not regret taking even though I am probably going to receive a bad grade from it. I like that there is almost equal value assigned to the rote memorisation aspect and the critical analysis aspect, so if you lose from one side, you might be able to gain from the other (which was what happened in my case.) Furthermore, in order to get perfect marks from this class, you have to excel in a variety of different formats of assignment and different modes of learning. Overall, I believe this both raises the standard for excellent marks, making them to be true signs of a good student/archaeologist; and provides enough leeway to be able to pick up slack in areas you might be more capable in. I can not for the life of me remember specific dates and names, which makes me a rather poor student in this course, but I do not regret taking it at all. I learned so much in other areas that I believe, on an existential level, this course more than makes up for the damage it might have done to my GPA.

instructor:
As a student of this course, I admired Ms. Gates with her challenging, motivating and  to-the-point questions. Secondly, she, as a notable scholar, took part in answering and contributing to the main questions of the discipline into which she tries effectively to teach and orient the students. 
Thirdly, with her orientation, I have had the chance to feed my other studies with abundant number of sources and academics about whom she knows great deal of professional information. Lastly, her personal and close relation to the participants made me feel that I had chosen the true MA programme  for my future career.
course:
Positively, the course is like an umbrella integrating all aspects of archaeological science for the students. Contribution by the experts of specific topics transformed an expectedly standard seminar into the one like a Munsell colour chart. I am indebted to the original person behind this course style. 
The negative aspect of the course was the neglect of some important study areas, as archaeology of India, China or even Iran, and as Islamic, Zoroastrian etc. archaeologies. 
I personally wanted to learn Ancient Greek or Latin epigraphy yet did not have the chance to delve into this topic, due to the absence of any expert on the topic. It is my greatest pity for the course.
